QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_64

question.text: Per the current NISM VIII workbook (pp.134–135), which set of thresholds is among the stock-derivatives eligibility criteria on Indian exchanges?

answer.text: MQSOS at least Rs 25 lakh and MWPL at least Rs 500 crore (legacy thresholds)
Market capitalization of at least Rs 10,000 crore and daily turnover of Rs 500 crore

Median Quarter Sigma Order Size (MQSOS) of at least Rs 75 lakh and Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL) of at least Rs 1500 crore, with the underlying being in the top-500 stocks and meeting the prescribed average daily delivery value criterion
Minimum 5 years of listing history and no corporate-governance violations

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM VIII workbook (pp.134–135, December 2025) raises the MQSOS threshold to at least Rs 75 lakh and the MWPL threshold to at least Rs 1500 crore for stock-derivatives eligibility, in addition to the top-500 stock selection and an average daily delivery value criterion of about Rs 35 crore. The earlier Rs 25 lakh / Rs 500 crore thresholds are the legacy rule and are no longer current. The Trap: The legacy Rs 25 lakh / Rs 500 crore framing is the most common distractor; market-cap-only and listing-history rules are not the SEBI eligibility test. Cross-Exam Context: NISM VIII covers equity-derivatives eligibility in detail; currency derivatives and interest-rate derivatives have different underlying eligibility rules.
